FRENCH POLICE INTELLIGENCE REPORT

Grenade Explosion on Szechuen Road Bridge

At 5.30 p.m. yesterday an unknown person,
dressed as a labourer, threw two grenades near Szechuen
Road Bridge. The missiles exploded in front of Carlowitz
and Company, 670 Szechuen Road. A Chinese Constable of the
S.M.P., a British subject, a Japanese and 8 Chinese
pedestrians were injured. The injured were removed to hospital
by the Police. No arrests were made.

For some time now, the S.M.P. have been making
careful searches on Szechuen Road Bridge and this may have
given rise to dissatisfaction among the pro-Japanese Associations
on the north side of the creek and may have provoked the attack.

The Labour Situation

The Federation of Charity Organizations, 35
Yunnan Road, in view of its financial difficulties, dismissed
40 men engaged on refugee relief work on September 15. The
Federation issued two months' pay to each worker as discharge
allowance.

On September 16 the worker held a meeting of
protest and demanded five months pay.

Yesterday two representatives of the workers
submitted the demand to the Federation which rejected it.

法国警务情报报告

四川路桥手榴弹爆炸事件

昨日下午5时30分，一名身份不明、身穿劳工服装的人在四川路桥附近投掷了两枚手榴弹。弹药在四川路670号嘉利洋行（Carlowitz and Company）门前爆炸。一名华籍巡捕（系英国臣民）、一名日本人及8名中国行人受伤。伤者由警方送往医院。未实施逮捕。

一段时间以来，工部局警务处一直在四川路桥进行严密搜查，这可能引起了河北岸亲日团体的不满，并可能由此引发了此次袭击。

劳工状况

慈善团体联合会（地址：云南路35号）鉴于其财政困难，于9月15日解雇了40名从事难民救济工作的人员。该联合会向每名工人发放了两个月的工资作为遣散费。

9月16日，工人们举行抗议集会，要求支付五个月的工资。

昨日，两名工人代表向联合会提交了这一要求，但被拒绝。

K. Murai

I beg to report the following:-

On the 16th inst. at 5.20p.m. while in my car No. 8062
travelling from South to North on Szechuen Road corner Soochow
Road, where a bomb was detonated near my car and about 3 or 4
seconds later another one was exploded, where upon I had my
nephew Kin Togi stop the car.

After ascertaining that we were uninjured and not seeing
any one about I instructed my nephew to continue, on the Szechuen
Road bridge we were stopped by the Centurys where a full report
was given.

One of the missiles from the bomb went through our wind
making a 2 inches hole.

Signed:- K. Murai.

〔此处转录不清〕
pages.zh:
K. Murai

谨报告如下：

本月16日下午5时20分，我驾驶车牌号为8062的汽车，在四川路与苏州路交界处由南向北行驶。此时，一枚炸弹在我车附近引爆，约3或4秒后，另一枚炸弹爆炸。随即，我让我的侄子 Kin Togi 停车。

在确认我们未受伤且周围未见任何人后，我指示侄子继续行驶。在四川路桥上，我们被世纪车队（Centurys，音译）拦下，并提交了完整报告。

炸弹的一块碎片击穿了我们的挡风玻璃，留下了一个2英寸的洞。

Komao Takaoka,residing No. 96 Tung Tsau Li,
Scott Road.
Japan
Central 17/9/38 //// J.D.C. Yoshinaga
translated

I was proceeding to my house on a public ricsha from South
to North along Szech:ien Road from Iwai & Co.,No. 99 Hankow Road
where I am employed and came to the intersection of Soochow Rd.
where I alighted from the ricsha and was about to pay the fare
to the puller at the West side corner of Szechuen Rd. near the
bridge at about 5.20p.m. 16/9/38, when I saw one bomb explode
with a loud explosion at a point about 5 metres East of where
I was standing. Then a black object,about 5 mili-metres in
length and about 3 mili-metres in width came towards me.
The occurrence was so sudden that I could not step aside
out of the course of the black object,whereupon a second ex-
plosion took place very near to me resulting in my sustaining
injuries on the face and under the right lower eyelid. As
the situation was dangerous,I hurriedly took cover in the
second floor of an empty house nearby by running up the stair-
case,but thinking it unsafe to stay there any longer,I rushed
to the bridge and explained the circumstances to the naval
sentries on duty who permitted me to cross over the bridge to
Hongkew area.
After returning to my home,at No. 96 Tung Tsau Li Scott
Road and,explaining how I sustained the injuries,I proceeded
to the Fooming Hospital where I received medical treatment.
Signed and chopped.

Komao Takaoka，居住于斯科特路（Scott Road）同兆里96号。
日本
中央巡捕房 1938年9月17日 //// J.D.C. Yoshinaga
翻译

我当时正乘坐公共黄包车，沿四川路由南向北，从我任职的汉口路99号岩井公司（Iwai & Co.）前往我家。当到达苏州路路口时，我于1938年9月16日下午5时20分左右，在靠近桥梁的四川路西侧拐角处下车，正准备向车夫支付车费。此时，我看见一枚炸弹在我站立位置以东约5米处爆炸，发出巨大的声响。随后，一个长约5毫米、宽约3毫米的黑色物体向我飞来。事发突然，我未能避开该黑色物体的轨迹，紧接着在我非常近的地方发生了第二次爆炸，导致我面部及右眼下眼睑受伤。鉴于情况危险，我迅速跑上附近一栋空房的楼梯，躲入二楼，但觉得在那里停留已不安全，便冲向桥梁，向执勤的海军哨兵说明情况，哨兵允许我过桥进入虹口地区。
回到斯科特路同兆里96号的家中，说明了受伤经过后，我前往福明医院（Fooming Hospital）接受了治疗。
签名并盖章。
〔此处转录不清〕

Vivian Lenoise
British (Canadian)                 D.S.I. Guess
Central           21/9/38           ---

My name is Vivien Lenoise,age 48 years,British,residing
at 681 Szechuen Road.
    At about 5.20p.m. on 16/9/38 I left my homeat 681 Szechuen
Road (this address being on the West side of Szechuen Road very
near the corner of Soochow Road) and proceeded to cross the
road towards the South east. As I gained the centre of the
roadway I heard a loud report as if from an explosion. I turned
round to see what had happened and at that time saw a large
dark coloured motor(closed) near the North-east corner of the
crossing Soochow-Szechuen Roads and proceeding east along
Soochow Road. At the same moment I saw a hand grenade,Mills
type,size about 5" x 3" oval shaped,rolling along the ground
from the North-east to the South-west direction of the road
intersection. Knowing that at the time of the explosion the bor
fragments would rise I threw myself on the ground but at approxi
mately that moment the explosion occurred and I was struck by
a piece of bomb fragment in the chin.
    Upon receiving the above injury I proceeded to the Navy 'Y'
Barber Shop and there asked my friend if there was a doctor in
the Navy 'Y' Building. I was informed that there was and there-
fore proceeded to see him. The bleeding from the wound was
persistent;however,and I was later taken to the General Hospita:
in the Emergency Ambulance.
    I did not see where the first bomb exploded but the second
bomb gave me my injury and also broke the window of my shop at
above address. I did not see any Japanese motor car or motor.
cycle in the vicinity at the time.
                The above is true.            Signed.
pages.zh:
Vivian Lenoise
英国籍（加拿大）                 D.S.I. Guess
中央巡捕房           1938年9月21日           ---

我叫 Vivien Lenoise，48岁，英国人，居住在四川路681号。
    1938年9月16日下午5时20分左右，我离开位于四川路681号的家（该地址位于四川路西侧，非常靠近苏州路路口），并向东南方向过马路。当我走到道路中央时，听到一声巨响，仿佛来自爆炸。我转身查看发生了什么事，当时看见一辆大型深色轿车（封闭式）靠近苏州路与四川路交叉口的东北角，并沿苏州路向东行驶。与此同时，我看见一枚米尔斯型（Mills type）手榴弹，呈椭圆形，尺寸约为5英寸 x 3英寸，沿地面从道路交叉口的东北方向向西南方向滚动。我知道爆炸时炸弹碎片会飞溅，便扑倒在地，但就在那一刻左右，爆炸发生，一块炸弹碎片击中了我的下巴。
    受上述伤后，我前往海军青年会（Navy 'Y'）理发店，询问我的朋友海军青年会大楼内是否有医生。得知有医生后，我便前去就诊。然而伤口持续出血，后来我被急救救护车送往总医院。
    我没有看到第一枚炸弹在哪里爆炸，但第二枚炸弹使我受伤，并震碎了我上述地址店铺的窗户。当时我在附近没有看到任何日本汽车或摩托车。
                以上属实。            签名。

pages.en:
Kazuo Takeuchi
Japan                                      xx   J.D.S. Kobayashi
Central Station       19-9-38              translated      Yoshinaga.

Report regarding my witnessing the bomb-thrower who is
responsible for the explosion on the South side of the Szechuen
Road Bridge on the 16-9-38.

    At about 5.20pm on the 16-9-38, I was chatting with Mr.
Morio Kobayashi, proprietor .. Kobayashi Yoko at his office
situated on the second floor of No. 673 Szechuen Road with my
eyes looking out onto the Szechuen Road through one of two
windows which were then left open, when I heard a loud explosion
in the direction of the Szechuen Road Bridge and, subsequently,
white smoke came in sight.

    While I was thinking that the noise was too loud for that
of puncture of motor-car tyre, I saw the Chinese crowd rush in
a Southerly direction along Szechuen Road. Now believing that
a bomb-explosion must have occurred, I rushed to the South side
one of the two windows standing up from the chair on which I
had been sitting, to see the situation downwards and looked
onto the road with my head stretched outward when I witnessed
a male Chinese, who had stood on the East side footpath of the
road directly opposite the window from which I was looking out,
threw a black object towards me immediately after pulling
something affixed on the object (which had been held in his right
hand) with his left hand swung thereto in same a manner as
pulling a thread. Simultaneously, a loud explosion was heard
which made me run into the inner part of the room urging Mr.
Kobayashi to follow me as it was considered dangerous to remain
close to the window.

    About 5 minutes afterwards, I re-approached the window

Kazuo Takeuchi
日本                                      xx   J.D.S. Kobayashi
中央巡捕房       1938年9月19日              翻译      Yoshinaga.

关于我目击1938年9月16日四川路桥南侧爆炸案投弹者的报告。

    1938年9月16日下午5时20分左右，我正与小林森雄（Morio Kobayashi）先生聊天，他是位于四川路673号二楼的小林洋行（Kobayashi Yoko）的店主。我的目光透过当时敞开的两扇窗户之一望向四川路，这时我听到四川路桥方向传来一声巨大的爆炸声，随后看到了白烟。

    当我心想这声音太大，不像是汽车轮胎爆胎的声音时，我看见人群沿着四川路向南奔跑。现在我确信一定发生了炸弹爆炸，于是我站起身，离开坐着的椅子，冲到南侧两扇窗户中的一扇前，探头向下观察路面情况。此时，我目睹了一名中国男子，站在与我探身观望的窗户正对面的路东人行道上，他用左手以类似拉线的方式拉动右手所持物体上的附属物，随即向我投掷了一个黑色物体。同时听到一声巨大的爆炸声，这让我跑进房间内部，并催促小林先生跟随我，因为靠近窗户被认为很危险。

    大约5分钟后，我再次靠近窗户

pages.en:
-2-

and looked outward again when I saw some Chinese police**〔此处转录不清〕**
south along Szechuen Road with pistols in their hands. For the
time being; I kept on looking outward, but suddenly recalling
that a truck was to come to under the office at 5.30p.m. even
date in response to a previous arrangement, and fearing that its
approach would probably be interrupted by the police cordon
thrown around the office, I went out of the office for the
purpose of informing the master of the transportation company
situated on Ningpo and Shansi Roads' corner to this effect and,
thereby, to postpone the despatch of the truck until the next
morning. On my way back to the office, I came to the corner of
Hongkong and Szechuen Roads where I was stopped by a policeman
posted on the said intersection to divert the traffic into the
police cordon.

In the meantime, Inspector Oikawa happened to pass by and,
after listening to my statement that I was wishing to return
to my office at No. 673 Szechuen Road and that I actually
witnessed from the window of the office, the person who threw
the bombs, managed to let me proceed through the cordon.

As to the description of the culprit, I can not give full
particulars of the person as I had a glance at him only, but I
consider that he was a youth of scholar type in outward appearance
aged 25 years or so and dressed in blue long gown.

Signed: Kazuo Takeuchi.
No.F10 Dong Kung Li,Woochang Rd.

向外张望，看见一些中国警察**〔此处转录不清〕**手持手枪沿四川路向南行进。暂时；我继续向外观看，但突然想起根据之前的安排，当天下午5时30分有一辆卡车要来办公室楼下，担心它的到来可能会因办公室周围设立的警察警戒线而受阻，我便走出办公室，目的是通知位于宁波路与山西路拐角的运输公司老板这一情况，从而将卡车的派遣推迟到第二天早上。在返回办公室的路上，我来到香港路与四川路的拐角处，被部署在该路口的一名警察拦下，他将交通分流至警察警戒线内。

在此期间，大川（Oikawa，音译）巡官恰好路过，在听取了我的陈述后——我希望返回四川路673号的办公室，且我确实从办公室窗口目击了投掷炸弹的人——他设法让我通过了警戒线。

关于罪犯的描述，由于我只瞥了他一眼，无法提供该人的全部详细特征，但我认为他是一名外表像书生型的青年，年龄约25岁，身穿蓝色长袍。

Lee Yung Tsong, C.P.C. 501 reports as follows:-
At 4p.m. on the 16th inst, I was on traffic duty at the

Between 3p.m. and 7p.m. on the 16th inst. I was on post duty

suddenly observed the clouds of smoke spreading in the vicinity

searching the man who was responsible for the throwing of the

vehicles and pedestrians to disperse in all directions and all
my efforts for finding the man were in vain. The above is my

| | At 5.22.p.m. on 16.9.1938 a telephone message was received from Mr.Andrews of Embankment Buildings, to the effect that an explosion had occurred outside Messrs Carlowitz on Szechuen Road and as a result the crowds were in a panic. Station alarms were sounded and all available men responded being followed shortly afterwards by the staff of C.8 under D.S.I.Crighton. | |

One of these, the first, had landed actually on Soochow Road slightly to the east of Szechuen Road, whilst the other which exploded a few seconds later had landed on Szechuen Road outside No.681 which is a few feet from the Soochow Road crossing. | |

| | 两枚炸弹被投掷在靠近苏州路的四川路上。1938年9月16日。 | |
| | 1938年9月16日下午5时22分，接到来自堤岸大厦（Embankment Buildings）安德鲁斯先生（Mr. Andrews）的电话消息，称四川路卡洛夫斯基洋行（Messrs Carlowitz）外发生爆炸，导致人群恐慌。警署拉响警报，所有可用警力随即出动，随后不久由C.8部门主管副督察克里顿（D.S.I. Crighton）率领该部门人员跟进。 | |

////// 宋书记员
翻译

1938年9月16日下午5时许，我在中山公园内等待领取薪水。出来时，我看到两名日本士兵驾驶一辆带边车的摩托车，由东向西高速行驶。几分钟后，我听到一声爆炸，随即升起一团烟雾。我向东奔跑，接着又听到另一声爆炸。当时我发现左脚受伤。之后由警察将我送往莱斯华医院治疗。

签名。

Oen Van Ling,22,Kompo,S/Tramcar employee,
Hart Rd. tram depot.

////    Clerk Sung
translated

At about 2p.m. I was operating as a switch man near the
Szechuen Rd. Bridge. At 5p.m. I was standing on the East side
of Szechuen Rd. about 10 yards off Soochow Rd. and I was facing
Northeast and was surrounded by pedestrians. I heard an
explosion and this made all pedestrians run in a disorderly
manner. I treated the explosion coolly because I believed it
originated from a burst ricsha tyre. However,another explosion
took place and I was then convinced that missiles were flung.
Nevertheless,I did not observe anyone throwing hand-grenades.
After taking refuge in a nearby un-occupied house I felt a
pain on my right arm and also discovered it bleeding. I then
reported this to a foreign policeman who sent me to the Lester
Chinese Hospital.

Signed.
pages.zh:
Oen Van Ling，22岁，籍贯 Kompo（音译），职业：电车员工，住赫德路电车车厂。

//// 宋书记员
翻译

下午2时许，我在四川路桥附近担任扳道工。下午5时，我站在四川路东面，距离苏州路约10码处，面朝东北，周围都是行人。我听到一声爆炸，导致所有行人慌乱奔逃。我对这次爆炸保持冷静，因为我以为是人包车轮胎爆裂所致。然而，接着发生了另一次爆炸，使我确信有人投掷了投射物。尽管如此，我没有看到任何人投掷手榴弹。在躲进附近一间无人居住的房屋后，我感到右臂疼痛，并发现其在流血。随后我向一名外籍警察报告，他将我送往莱斯华医院。

签名。

C.P.C. 2728

/////     Clerk Sung
translated

At about 5.10p.m. 16/9/38 I was on duty at Szechuen Rd.
Bridge,when I heard an explosion. I immediately produced my
service pistol and following this another explosion took place.
Pedestrians ran away in confusion and I failed to discover the
criminal(s). I then attended the wounded persons until S.F.
Ambulance arrived. The injured persons were removed to Lester
Chinese Hospital for treatment.

Signed.

1938年9月16日下午5时10分许，我正在四川路桥执勤，此时听到一声爆炸。我立即拔出佩枪，随后又发生了一次爆炸。行人混乱逃散，我未能发现罪犯。随后我照料伤者，直到圣约翰救护队（S.F. Ambulance）抵达。伤者被送往莱斯华医院接受治疗。

//////      Clerk Sung
translated

Sung Ah Kung,41,Kompo,S/Hawker,66 Mohawk Rd.
At about 4p.m. 16/9/38 I left home and proceeded to the Chinese
Gardens on Soochow Rd. with a view to collecting secondhand goods.
However,when I was proceeding W.- E. along Soochow Rd. I heard
two explosions and started to run in an easterly direction.
After running for a few paces I felt a pain in my legs. I there-
fore sat down on the ground and ascertained the nature of my
injures, I believed that hand-grenades had been thrown. I was
later sent to Lester Chinese Hospital by a C.P.C.
                                Signed.

Sung Ah Kung，41岁，籍贯 Kompo（音译），职业：小贩，住莫霍克路（Mohawk Rd.）66号。

////// 宋书记员
翻译

Sung Ah Kung，41岁，籍贯 Kompo（音译），职业：小贩，住莫霍克路66号。
1938年9月16日下午4时许，我离家前往苏州路的中山公园，打算收集旧货。然而，当我沿苏州路由西向东行走时，听到两声爆炸，便开始向东奔跑。跑了几步后，我感到腿部疼痛。于是我坐在地上检查伤势，我认为有人投掷了手榴弹。后来由一名中国巡捕（C.P.C.）将我送往莱斯华医院。

Ka Za,Chungking Rd.

////          Clerk Sung
translated

At about 5.15p.m. today I was proceeding along Soochow Rd. E. to
W. and when nearing Szechuen Rd. Bridge I heard an explosion. I
therefore turned back and started to run. At that time another
explosion occurred and I felt pain on my right leg. I fell onto
the ground and was later sent to Lester Chinese Hospital by

                                Signed.

//// 宋书记员
翻译

今天下午5时15分许，我正沿苏州路由东向西行走，当接近四川路桥时，听到一声爆炸。于是我转身开始奔跑。当时又发生了一次爆炸，我感到右腿疼痛。我倒在地上，后来由警察送往莱斯华医院。我没有看到是谁投掷了投射物。

Koo Ah Hwo,17,Ningpo,S/Unemployed,30 Sung
Yue Li,Rue Lafayette F.C.

////      Clerk Sung
translated

At about 3p.m. 16/9/38 I left home and intended to visit my
friend named Bao Kwei Dong at Museum Rd. However, I did not
know where Museum Rd. is. I proceeded on Yu Ya Ching Rd. and
turning into Soochow Rd. I walked W. to E. until I arrived at
Szechuen Rd. Bridge where I turned and walked in a southerly
direction along Szechuen Rd. It was about 5p.m.,and the thorough-
fare was crowded with pedestrians,who were mostly coolies
coming from Hongkew. When I was walking on the East side of
Szechuen Rd. I heard an explosion emerging from behind,and this
resulted in a melee. As I was also panic-striken I ran after
the crowd. After running a few paces I heard a second
explosion,but I continued to run in a southerly direction. When
reaching Hongkong and Szechuen Rds corner I encountered two
Sikh police who on seeing blood stains on my pants stopped me
and hired a public ricsha,by which I was sent to Central Police
Station. On arrival at the station, I was in turn sent to
Lester Chinese Hospital. I did not observe the bomb thrower(s).
                                Signed.
pages.zh:
Koo Ah Hwo，17岁，籍贯宁波，职业：无业，住法租界霞飞路（Rue Lafayette F.C.）松月里30号。

//// 宋书记员
翻译

1938年9月16日下午3时许，我离家打算去博物馆路拜访名为 Bao Kwei Dong 的朋友。但是，我不知道博物馆路在哪里。我走到虞洽卿路，转入苏州路，由西向东行走，直到到达四川路桥，然后转弯沿四川路向南行走。当时约为下午5时，街道上挤满了行人，大多是从虹口来的苦力。当我走在四川路东侧时，听到身后传来一声爆炸，这引起了一阵混乱。我也惊慌失措，跟随人群奔跑。跑了几步后，我听到第二声爆炸，但我继续向南奔跑。当到达香港路与四川路转角时，我遇到两名锡克教警察，他们看到我裤子上的血迹后拦住了我，并雇了一辆公共人包车，将我送往中央捕房。到达捕房后，我又被转送往莱斯华医院。我没有观察到投掷炸弹者。
签名。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Tsang Ah Siau ( )
native of Luiho taken by me D.S.I.Guess
at Lester Hosp. on the 16.9.1938 and interpreted by Clerk Woo

My name is Tsang Ah Siau, age 17, Native of Luiho, Single,
carpenter, residing at No.111, Lane 1536 Sinza Road.

Between 16.8.1938 and 14.9.1938 I was employed working in
Woosung. On 14.9.1938 I returned to my home and on the afternoon
of 16.9.1938 a foreman of my ex-employer call on me and told me
to collect my wages from Koo Ah Hwo ( ) at Garden Bridge
that afternoon. At about 4.p.m., therefore, I left my home and
walked towards Garden Bridge. I proceeded along Soochow Road
and was about to cross Szechuen Road when I was stopped as a
milkless car was turning. After the car had turned I was again
about to cross the road when a motor cycle, khaki in colour,
driven by a Japanese and with a Japanese passenger in the side-
car was coming from the opposite direction (east to west) and
was turning North to cross Szechuen Bridge. As it made the turn
there was a loud bang which was followed a few seconds later
later by another similar noise. There were many people in the
vicinity and all started to run and I was pushed and ran in an
Easterly direction for a short distance before I was blinded by
the blood which came from a wound over my eye. Until then I did
not know I had been injured. I stayed where I was and was later
found by the Police and taken to hospital.

The two Japanese on the motor cycle were dressed in
Khaki uniforms and small khaki cloth caps. I did not see whether
either of them actually threw the missile but same was thrown
very near to their machine. I cannot say by whom or from where
either of the bombs were thrown.

This is statement is true.

Signed Tsang Ah Siau.
Thumbprinted.

以下是由副督察 Guess 于1938年9月16日在莱斯医院对籍贯 Luiho（音译）的 Tsang Ah Siau（ ）进行的陈述记录，由伍书记员翻译。

我叫 Tsang Ah Siau，17岁，籍贯 Luiho（音译），未婚，木匠，住新闸路1536弄111号。

1938年8月16日至1938年9月14日期间，我在吴淞受雇工作。1938年9月14日我回到家中，1938年9月16日下午，我前雇主的一名工头来访，告诉我当天下午去外白渡桥向 Koo Ah Hwo（ ）领取工资。因此，下午4时许，我离家向外白渡桥走去。我沿苏州路前行，正要穿过四川路时，因一辆汽车正在转弯而被拦住。汽车转弯后，我正准备再次过马路，此时一辆卡其色的摩托车由对面（由东向西）驶来，驾驶员为日本人，边车上坐着一名日本乘客，该摩托车正转向北以穿过四川路桥。就在它转弯时，发出了一声巨响，几秒后又传来另一声类似的响声。附近有很多人，大家都开始奔跑，我被推搡着向东跑了一小段距离，随后眼睛上方的伤口流出的血使我视线模糊。在此之前，我并不知道自已受了伤。我留在原地，后来被警察发现并送往医院。

摩托车上的两名日本人穿着卡其色制服，戴着小的卡其色布帽。我没有看到他们中是否有人实际投掷了投射物，但投射物是在离他们的车辆很近的地方投掷的。我无法说明炸弹是由谁或从哪里投掷的。

此陈述属实。

Tsang Ah Siau 签名。

Tsepoo Rd.

////          Clerk Sung
translated

At about 5p.m. 16/9/38 I was proceeding to visit my relatives at
House 24 Alcock Rd.,Hongkew District. As I was proceeding near
Szechuen Rd. Bridge I observed two Japanese soldiers driving a
m/bicycle with side car E. to W. along Soochow Rd. at full speed.
At that time I was outside the Chinese Public Gardens & I heard
an explosion. Following this I felt something strike my abdomen. I
then started to run and heard another explosion. I did not stop

my friend at 128 Museum Rd. Later I went to Central Police Stn.

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.
0043
SEP 1 7 1938

11 Injured By
2 Bombs On
Soochow Road

Vivian Lenoise Wounded
On Chin; Japanese
Also Hurt

Eleven persons, including one British subject, nine Chinese pedestrians and one Japanese, sustained injuries to varying degrees of seriousness when two hand-grenades of the Mills type were thrown on Soochow Road directly south of the Szechuen Road Bridge at 5.20 p.m. yesterday.

Mr. Vivian Lenoise, well-known local football referee, is the wounded British subject. He was struck on the chin by a piece of flying bomb fragment. The resulting wound was a severe gash. It was not serious enough to keep him confined to the hospital and he was sent home after treatment.

One of the wounded Chinese is a woman who sustained severe cuts about the legs. She was crossing the intersection of Soochow and Szechuen Roads when the explosions occurred. The other wounded Chinese are all men.

Victim May Lose Eye

Seven sustained superficial wounds about the arms and face and were all sent home from the Lester Chinese Hospital after receiving first aid treatment. The eighth wounded Chinese is in a serious condition and may lose the sight of his right eye. He was rendered unconscious when struck by a bomb fragment and was still in a state of coma at a late hour last night.

The wounded Japanese was a civilian pedestrian, according to all information available last night. He was not badly injured.

Coming one after another, the two explosions created a panic in the Szechuen Road area south of the bridge. Pedestrians scattered in all directions as flying bomb splinters sprayed the side of the building occupied by Carlowitz and Company.

Within a matter of four minutes, detectives and a special squad of police from the Central Station had arrived at the scene. The police reserves with their big red "wagons" made the trip from Gordon Road to the bridge in the fast time of seven minutes. The street was blocked off and investigation started on the spot.

Immediately after the bombing, however, Japanese military sentries closed the bridge to all traffic. Only wounded Mr. Lenoise and the wounded Japanese, accompanied by Settlement police officers, were permitted to cross the bridge as they proceeded to the General Hospital.

Motorcar Hit

The first of the two bombs landed on Soochow Road near the Carlowitz and Company building. An automobile, driven by Mr. W. Mohr, German, had just completed crossing the bridge from north to south and was turning east on Soochow Road when the blast occurred. The machine was struck by flying splinters but fortunately Mr. Mohr escaped uninjured.

Mr. Mohr immediately pulled over to the curb and parked his machine. In the meantime, the second bomb exploded. This missile landed in front of a small exchange and cigarette shop at the corner of Soochow and Szechuen Roads.

Up to a late hour last night, detectives engaged in investigating the case had made but little progress in their efforts to determine the identity of the bomb-tossers.

According to one Japanese who claimed to have been an eye-witness, a tall Chinese of the student type threw the bombs. The man swore that he saw the bombs thrown.

Another eye-witness, a Chinese is said to have informed the police that the bomb-tosser was dressed in foreign clothes. The same witness also was positive that the man was not a Chinese.

Still another report circulated last night was to the effect that the bombs were tossed from a speeding motorcar. Later, another report was to the effect that they had been thrown by a man riding a motorcycle.

In view of these conflicting reports, the police found themselves at a loss in their attempts to obtain even so much as an ordinary description of the bomb thrower or bomb throwers.

One theory advanced late last night was to the effect that the intended victim was a "Ta Tao" official. It was stated that the bomb-tosser had waited on the south side of the bridge for the official to cross and that when the latter put in his appearance, the bomb was thrown. No "Ta Tao" officials, however, were among the wounded.

（手写批注：S / 75 / +2）
（底部手写签名：Lee C'9）

0043
1938年9月17日

苏州路上两枚炸弹致11人受伤

Vivian Lenoise 下巴受伤；一名日本人也受伤

昨日下午5时20分，两枚米尔斯型（Mills type）手榴弹被投掷在四川路桥正南面的苏州路上，造成11人受伤，伤情轻重不一，其中包括一名英国臣民、九名中国行人和一名日本人。

Vivian Lenoise 先生是当地著名的足球裁判，也是受伤的英国臣民。他被一块飞溅的炸弹碎片击中下巴，造成严重裂伤。伤势并未严重到需要住院，他在接受治疗后被送回家中。

受伤的中国公民中有一名妇女，腿部遭受严重割伤。爆炸发生时，她正穿过苏州路与四川路的交叉口。其他受伤的中国公民均为男性。

受害者可能失明

七人手臂和面部受轻伤，在莱斯华医院接受急救处理后均被送回家中。第八名受伤的中国公民情况严重，可能会失去右眼视力。他被炸弹碎片击中后昏迷，直至昨晚深夜仍处于昏迷状态。

根据昨晚掌握的所有信息，受伤的日本人是一名平民行人。他受伤不重。

两次爆炸接连发生，在桥南的四川路地区引起了恐慌。飞溅的炸弹碎片喷洒在卡尔洛维茨公司（Carlowitz and Company）所占用的建筑物侧面，行人四处逃散。

在四分钟内，来自中央捕房的侦探和特别警察小队已抵达现场。警察后备队开着大型红色“警车”，仅用七分钟便从戈登路（Gordon Road）赶到了桥头。街道被封锁，现场调查随即开始。

然而，轰炸发生后，日本军事哨兵立即封锁了桥梁，禁止所有交通通行。只有受伤的 Lenoise 先生和受伤的日本人，在租界警察的陪同下，在被送往总医院途中获准过桥。

汽车被击中

两枚炸弹中的第一枚落在苏州路上，靠近卡尔洛维茨公司大楼。德国人 W. Mohr 先生驾驶的一辆汽车刚刚由北向南穿过大桥，正要在苏州路上向东转弯时，爆炸发生了。车辆被飞溅的碎片击中，但幸运的是 Mohr 先生未受伤。

Mohr 先生立即将车靠边停放。与此同时，第二枚炸弹爆炸。这枚投射物落在苏州路与四川路转角的一家小型兑换处兼香烟店门前。

截至昨晚深夜，负责调查此案的侦探在确定投弹者身份方面进展甚微。

据一名自称目击者的日本人称，是一名身材高大、学生模样的中国人投掷了炸弹。此人发誓说他看到了炸弹被投掷的过程。

另一名目击者，一名中国人，据称告知警察，投弹者穿着西式服装。同一位目击者还肯定地说，那人不是中国人。

昨晚流传的另一种说法是，炸弹是从一辆疾驰的汽车上投下的。后来，又有说法称是由一名骑摩托车的人投掷的。

鉴于这些相互矛盾的报告，警方在试图获取哪怕是对投弹者的一般描述时也感到束手无策。

昨晚深夜提出的一种理论认为，预定受害者是一名“大陶”（Ta Tao，音译）官员。据说投弹者在桥南侧等待该官员过桥，当后者出现时，炸弹被投出。然而，伤者中并没有“大陶”官员。

（手写批注：S / 75 / +2）
（底部手写签名：Lee C'9）

My name is Fang Ping Van, namely Hsu Au Wei, age 22,

Standard publishes the following letter sent by one Hsu Au-wei
(許下幃)： 11.5.38(00)

THE FINDING OF A BOMB NEAR WING ON BUILDING AT CORNER
OF CHEKIANG AND KIUKIANG ROADS

"To the editor,
"The report published in your newspaper on
the discovery of a hand grenade beneath a public ricsha
near the Wing On building is a little inconsistent with
the facts. I, the writer,happened to pass by the place at
the time and witnessed the affair. The missile apparently
was thrown from a high place and made a noise when it
struck the ground only 5 feet away from me, but fortunately
it did not explode. I did not realize the fact until
somebody raised an alarm and said that the thing was a hand
grenade. I then began to run fearing lest a second or
even a third hand grenade might come. On considering
the matter later I could not guess the object of the bomb
thrower because at that time no vehicles carrying notable
persons were in the vicinity. It might be said that
the bomb was thrown with no other object but to endanger
peace and order.
"The time when the bomb was discovered by a
beggar under a public ricsha was placed by your newspaper
at about 9 p.m., but actually the missile was hurled down
at 8.40 p.m."

THE RELIEF OF REFUGEES

The Chinese people should be grateful to the

Sir,
At 8.45 p.m. on the 9-5-38, C.P.C. 1596 reported by telephone that a hand-grenade had been found on Chekiang Road near Kiukiang Road.

The hand-grenade was placed in a bucket of water and in order to secure same in an immovable position a quantity of sand was poured in the bucket.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 10 MAY 1938）
Enquiries were made in the vicinity when a number of people were questioned, but this proved fruitless in obtaining any information regarding the identity of the person who had placed the hand-grenade on the roadway.

Yamasaki of the Japanese Gendarmerie came to the Station and asked to give them particulars regarding the time and place where the hand-grenade was found also enquired if an arrest was made in this case. They were supplied with a brief outline of the occurrence.
The hand-grenade will be kept at this Station, pending instruction regarding the disposal of same.

7 Wounded By
Grenade On
Kwangse Road

Another Hurled At Tien-
tsin Road Fails To
Explode

Seven persons, all Chinese, were
injured about ten o'clock last night
when an unknown person threw a
bomb of the "potato-masher" type
from the top of a building on
Kwangse Road near Nanking Road.
The bomb hit the pavement, ex-
ploding and sending fragments of
shrapnel over a fairly wide area.
Two of the persons injured sus-
tained serious wounds and were
transported to the hospital by emer-
gency ambulance.
Police on duty nearby immediately
turned in an alarm and reserve
units with the red riot wagons were
rushed to the scene. Nanking
Road between Chekiang and Kwang-
se Roads was roped off and all ricksha
and foot traffic was brought to a
halt.
Tram cars and busses were per-
mitted to pass through the police
lines but all other vehicles, excep-
tion official motorcars, were de-
toured around Chekiang Road.

Buildings Searched

All shops in the district just
roped off were closed while police
search parties went through the
buildings. It was understood that
no arrests had been made up to a
late hour last night although the
searches were carried on until al-
most midnight.
The police had no theories as to
who might have thrown the bomb.
There were no Japanese soldiers or
bluejackets in the area at the time
and besides, the bomb was not
thrown direct on Nanking Road.
A detachment of the Seaforth
Highlanders occupied the area at
about 11.00 p.m. and remained on
guard there last night as an as-
surance of protection to the resid-
ents in the vicinity of the bombing.
The missile struck the pavement
between the Sincere and Sun Sun
Department Stores about 60 feet
from Nanking Road and the only
people in this area at the time
were Chinese pedestrians.
In roping off the area on Nan-
king Road, the police were success-
ful in isolating the department stores
and it was believed that the guilty
person or persons might be appre-
hended.

Bomb Fails To Explode

One other bomb was thrown last
evening. This missile was heaved
by some unknown person at the
corner of Tientsin and Kiangse
Roads, at 7.30 p.m. It failed to
explode.
The missile was picked up by a
Chinese constable and is now in
the hands of detectives of the Cen-
tral Station who are engaged in
investigating the case.

七人在
广西路
被手榴弹炸伤

另一枚投往天
津路的手榴弹
未爆炸

昨晚十时许，一名不明身份者从靠近南京路的广西路某建筑物顶部投下一枚“土豆捣碎器”式（即柄式）炸弹，导致七人受伤，伤者均为中国人。炸弹击中人行道后爆炸，弹片飞溅至相当广泛的区域。两名伤者伤势严重，由急救救护车送往医院。
附近执勤警察立即发出警报，配备红色防暴车的后备部队迅速赶至现场。浙江路与广西路之间的南京路路段被警戒线封锁，所有人力车和行人交通被迫停止。
电车和公共汽车获准穿过警方警戒线，但除官方机动车外，所有其他车辆均被改道绕行浙江路。

搜查建筑物

警方搜查队进入建筑物搜查期间，刚被警戒线封锁区域内的所有商店均已关闭。据悉，尽管搜查持续至接近午夜，但直至昨晚深夜仍未实施逮捕。
警方对于谁可能投掷炸弹没有任何推测。当时该地区没有日本士兵或水兵，此外，炸弹并非直接投掷在南京路上。
海福特高地团的一支分队于晚上约11点进驻该区域，并昨晚在那里驻守警卫，以保障轰炸附近居民的安全。
导弹击中先施百货公司和苏孙百货公司之间的人行道，距离南京路约60英尺，当时该区域仅有的行人是中国路人。
通过在南京路设置警戒线，警方成功隔离了各家百货公司，据信这可能有助于 apprehend（逮捕）肇事者。

炸弹未爆炸

昨晚还投下了另一枚炸弹。这枚导弹于晚上7点30分被某不明身份者投掷在天津路与江西路（Kiangse Roads）转角处。它未能爆炸。
该导弹由一名中国巡捕拾获，目前由中央巡捕房的侦探保管，他们正在调查此案。
